newsitem.title: NORWAY: US troops could return to Bosnia if needed-- Perry.
newsitem.headline: US troops could return to Bosnia if needed-- Perry.

text.p: U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Thursday Washington will strongly consider sending American troops back into Bosnia next year if NATO deems it "necessary and appropriate."
Alliance defence ministers have ordered a study of missions and risks for any new NATO force in Bosnia next year, after the mandate of the current U.S.-led international force expires in December.

Allied pressure has been mounting on the U.S. France, Germany, Denmark and Norway have virtually promised to join any new military force replacing the current 52-000-member international peace implementation force (IFOR). Russsia has also expressed strong interest.
The United States, with 15,000 troops in the current force, has been reluctant to make any decision until the mission is fully defined.
Commitment to such a force could be a chancy political move for incumbent President Bill Clinton ahead of the November 5 U.S. presidential election.

"The United States is not prepared to make a commitment at this time, but we are prepared to consider participating if the NATO study shows that our involvement is necessary and appropriate," Perry told a news conference.
